excerpt: Flawrence finds security vulnerabilities in source code with LLM agents. It reads a codebase, builds a threat model, maps the attack surface and gives every entry point its own research agent. A second agent validates each candidate finding and tries to reproduce it. Only findings with a verified reproducer are submitted. A proof of concept is then written for each one. Flawrence is written in Rust. It works with Anthropic, OpenAI, Cloudflare Workers AI and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The bugs Flawrence has found so far are listed in FINDINGS.md. Warning Agents run shell commands, build the target and execute proofs of concept. Run Flawrence in a container or a VM. Never point it at a machine you care about. A full review fans out to many agents and can cost a lot of tokens. Set MAX_COST_USD. We recommend, running flawrence with locally hosted open-weight models to get the maximum out of it. cargo build --release export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... target/release/flawrence-runner --agent security-review \ --directory /path/to/target --artifacts out \ "Review this codebase for security issues" The runner loads a .env file from the working directory. Copy .env.example to .env to get started. Every agent names a default model in its definition. Use --model <provider>/<model> to override it for one run, or set FLAWRENCE_MODEL. The security-review agent runs this pipeline. - threat-model describes the application, its attackers and its trust boundaries. - attack-surface lists every function an attacker can reach. - test-idiom finds a reliable way to run small reproducers against the target. - One vulnerability-research agent runs per attack surface entry. It writes a finding_* artifact for every candidate. - vulnerability-validation checks each finding and rejects false positives. - vulnerability-poc writes and runs a proof of concept for each confirmed vulnerability. - dedup_check drops duplicates. submit_finding stores the rest under <artifacts>/submitted/…
